To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CFIR was a useful framework in assessing the implementation context of the QI program in Kano.
the QI program was implemented in an enabling environment with a high level of health workers confidence in it and that the implementation context is characterized by both facilitators and barriers.

1) The CFIR framework was useful for guiding a systematic evaluation of implementation context of the QI program; 2) Health workers reported higher score in two facilities (PHC1 and PHC5) for the QI across all domains of CFIR; and 3) Health workers reported implementation barriers such as vaccine stock out, and lack of incentives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a theory driven framework for formative evaluation in QI program implementation.
the use of theory driven formative assessment to generate rapid feedback to inform QI program implementation in a low resource health care setting.
the implementation context of QI interventions in a low resource context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study demonstrated the value of using theory based evaluation in QI programs to generate feedback that can be integrated into subsequent PDSA cycles.
this study demonstrated the value of theory driven formative assessment of QI implementation context in a low resource settings.
CFIR can be used to systematically evaluate the implementation context of QI programs and can be used to inform the design of subsequent cycles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CFIR can be used to guide formative evaluation of QI programs in low resource settings.

the CFIR can be used to systematically evaluate the implementation context of QI programs in low and middle income countries.
